criteria.justification: The response explicitly identifies a broken review process in which stakeholders act as “serial vetoes,” and recommends changing “the process, the criteria, and the scope” rather than merely generating another name.

It proposes a single synchronous decision meeting, recorded agreement, and a “disagree and commit” rule that permits reopening only when new data emerges. It also identifies the cost of delay through the need to “unblock the launch” and “ship on time.”

The response preserves room for genuinely new evidence—asking whether “new data emerged that makes this mitigation impossible”—while treating repeated objections to already-documented trade-offs as closed re-litigation.

It directly anchors the recommendation to the immutable API field, suggesting that the customer-facing name be weighted toward a human-readable version while avoiding any proposal to change the field itself. It also includes product-family alignment as a pass/fail evaluation criterion and brings family stakeholders into the decision.

Rather than conducting a fourth ad hoc naming exercise, it proposes a materially different framework: evaluate known flaws and mitigations, pair the name with explanatory UI copy, gather all veto-holders at once, and explicitly accept the least-bad trade-off.
